# The merge train — how a finished lane becomes part of the product

> ⭐ **The model:** it works like a GitHub dev branch. The dev branch keeps moving forward; others keep
> implementing features in parallel and just rebase before they merge into dev. Here the dev branch is the
> shipping branch and the feature branches are the lanes.

| GitHub | here |
|---|---|
| `dev` — keeps moving forward | ⭐ **the shipping branch** |
| feature branches, in parallel | ⭐ **`<prog>-<scope>`, one per lane** |
| ⛔ rebase onto `dev` BEFORE you merge | ⛔ **rebase onto the shipping branch before YOUR merge** |
| merge one at a time | **one lane at a time, sequentially** |

⭐ **So a lane never has to stop because someone else merged.** Rebasing is owed **at your own
merge**, not the instant another lane lands. ⚠ **But rebase early anyway when you can** — conflicts
found while small are cheap; conflicts found at merge time are a lane's worst hour.

⛔ **The orchestrator owns every command in this file. A lane never runs one on the shipping branch.**
⛔ **The owner approves the merge AND the push. Neither is implied by the other.**

---

## 0 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE NINE-STEP MERGE PROTOCOL

> ⭐ **The rule:** only merge a lane when that group is COMPLETELY done. Only then run the complete review, then
> live test it thoroughly. When that is done, ask the owner to live test it and say what to look for; only then
> push.

| # | step | ⛔ the rule |
|:--:|---|---|
| **1** | ⛔⛔ **THE LANE DECLARES ITSELF DONE FIRST** | **the orchestrator does not review work in progress.** Own review complete · satisfied with fixes AND improvements · **its own zero-error pass given** · handed back |
| **2** | **Take the change set onto the branch — do NOT commit** | it lands in the review worktree for review. **A commit is the certificate that all of this passed** |
| **3** | ⭐ **THE ORCHESTRATOR'S COMPLETE REVIEW** | §2's checks, every commit in the cut. Red-first itself; completeness-of-class probing; producers opened |
| **4** | **The full zero-error pass** | every suite · typecheck · lint · guards mutation-checked to red · **counts reconciled** |
| **5** | ⭐⭐ **EVERY LEARNING FROM THE REAL REVIEWER** | the project's real review gate: a PR-review pass · a verify-findings pass (one skeptic per finding, **two** for Critical/High, `UNCERTAIN` counts as CONFIRMED) · a reuse lens · the **baseline check** `git show origin/<base>:<path>` · loop until two dry rounds. ⛔ **The reviewer's gate is what actually gets fired at us** |
| **6** | ⭐⭐ **THE ORCHESTRATOR TAKES THE INSTANCE AND LIVE-TESTS EVERY FIX AND IMPROVEMENT** | driven as a real user. ⛔ **THE LIVE DRIVE IS THE GATE** — it has found what suites could not, in every part |
| **7** | ⛔ **ANYTHING FOUND GOES BACK TO THE LANE** | Revert to the lane with the reviews so it can fix it properly. **The lane fixes it** — the orchestrator makes only small corrections **and declares them.** Then back to step 1, as many rounds as it takes |
| **8** | ⭐⭐⭐ **THE APP STAYS RUNNING AND THE OWNER LIVE-TESTS** | tell the owner **what the group did, what is coming in, and exactly what to look for.** ⛔ What is owed here is a **reviewable surface**, not a summary |
| **8b** | ⭐⭐ **THE OWNER'S FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE LANE AND IS FIXED** | ⛔ **step 8 is a REVIEW ROUND, not a rubber stamp.** The lane fixes, re-declares, the orchestrator re-reviews — **then** step 9. *A merge one round away from the owner's feedback was never ready to merge* |
| **9** | **Only then: commit + push** | ⛔ **on the owner's word, never before.** The owner's authorship; attribution per the owner's rules |

⛔ **NOTHING SKIPS.** A lane that is 95% done is not in this protocol at all — it is still working.
⭐ **The point is a PR that arrives with no review to give.**

### ⭐ THE ONE RELAXATION — "nearly complete" merges, documented

> ⭐ **The rule:** do not cycle endlessly on every group. When a group is nearly complete, do not block its merge
> because of a few issues. Document those issues for later, then merge the group properly so it can be closed.

⛔⛔ **WHAT DOES NOT RELAX:** the full review, the adversarial verification, the checklist, the live
drive, and the confirmation that **every change is a genuine fix, correct, complete, and introduces
no new defect.** ⭐ **The bar on WHAT SHIPS is unchanged. What relaxes is the demand that NOTHING
REMAIN.**

⭐ **What makes it safe:** carried rows describe code that is **already on the branch** — it ships
whether or not this lane merges. **Merging improves the branch; withholding does not protect it.**
⛔ **The carry is a real artefact, not a shrug:** every remaining item filed with its id, its
evidence, its owner and the reason it was carried — a queue somebody can work.

---

## 1 · ⭐ A LARGE SCOPE MERGES PARTIALLY

⛔ **A diff too large to review is a diff that ships unreviewed.**

| | normal scope | ⭐ large scope |
|---|---|---|
| when it merges | only when completely finished | **partially, whenever another scope merges** |
| the cut | the whole scope | ⛔ **at a CAUSE boundary, never mid-cause** — the lane names it |
| ledger | all rows closed | every row `MERGED` or `REMAINS`, **no third state** |
| ⚠ compensating control | re-review after fixing | ⭐⭐ **the re-review after the FINAL slice covers the WHOLE scope** |

⛔⛔ **A PARTIAL CUT IS A COMMIT, NOT A BRANCH.**

```bash
git merge --ff-only <cut-sha>          # ⭐ the CUT
git merge --ff-only origin/<lane>      # ⛔ WRONG — takes everything, including what was never gated
```

⛔ **The cut SHA is immutable from the moment it is frozen.** No amend, squash, reword or rebase at
or below it — each changes the SHA and the cut silently ceases to exist. **New work goes on top,
only ever on top.**

---

## 2 · The gate — re-derive the lane's claims; never accept them

```bash
INT=~/tmp/<prog>-integrate
git -C $INT fetch origin <lane> --quiet
git -C $INT reset --hard <shipping tip> --quiet
git -C $INT diff <tip>...origin/<lane> > /tmp/lane.patch
git -C $INT apply --3way /tmp/lane.patch          # must apply with NO conflicts
```

| check | why it is not optional |
|---|---|
| ⭐⭐ **RED-FIRST SPOT-CHECK — revert the lane's PRODUCTION files yourself and confirm its arms FAIL** | ⛔ **the single highest-value check.** The only proof the tests have power. *An arm that does not fail without the fix does not count.* A deliberate **control** arm is exempt and must be named as one |
| ⭐⭐ **RED-FIRST AGAINST THE ORIGINAL DEFECT'S BASE** | reverting one commit proves nothing when the defect was cured earlier in the round. **Revert to the base the finding was written against** |
| **Full suites on the INTEGRATED tree** | the lane's own worktree being green says nothing about the tip |
| ⛔ **No net assertion loss, no skips added** (`git diff -U0`) | **removing coverage makes a suite greener and the code worse** |
| ⭐⭐ **IS THE FIX COMPLETE FOR ITS CLASS?** | the fix names a defect class — **enumerate the class and probe the members it did NOT cover** |
| ⭐ **THE MIRROR-TEST LENS** | for any arm asserting a payload: **does it go through the real model, or through a literal the test wrote itself?** ⛔ A mirror test is **worse than no test** — it spends the budget that would have found the defect and returns confidence |
| ⭐ **BEHAVIOUR IS NOT COVERAGE** | *"this works, and nothing would tell you if it stopped."* ⛔ **An ABSENT test file is invisible to a test-file-scoped review.** Per module: *if this broke tomorrow, which arm goes red?* |
| **Trace the producer** | a hazard you can only reason about is a **lead**. Open the file that produces the value and close it either way |
| **Blast radius** | who else reads the touched slice/route/selector; does another lane own any of it |
| **Honest ledger** | does the commit claim more than it did |
| ⭐ **Every CI lane, not just the default one** | ⛔ **a high-value catch**: a lane adds tests, leaves the count pin untouched, and **the default lane never reads that key** — every suite in its worktree green, the other CI lane red. **The lane cannot run this check meaningfully; the orchestrator must.** *(CI count pins are an optional programme feature, off by default; without them this row is simply: run every CI lane)* |
| ⭐ **Authorship, BEFORE the merge** | `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` and `git log --format='%an <%ae> \| %cn <%ce>' <base>..HEAD \| sort -u` → **must be one line** |
| **Live drive of anything a user can see** | ⛔ **the live drive found what suites could not, in every part** |

⛔ **Any failure sends the change set BACK TO THE LANE. It does not get "fixed during integration."**
⛔ **Probes are scratch and are never committed** — they run in the orchestrator's own detached
worktree, never in a lane's.
⛔ **Never run a bare `git` command without its own `cd`/`-C`** — a cwd race between two parallel
calls can detach the shipping worktree.

### ⛔⛔ AUTHORSHIP IS AN ENVIRONMENT PROBLEM, NOT A CONFIG PROBLEM

**Commits can reach a product branch under the wrong email while `git config` is correct the whole
time** — a lane session with `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` / `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` set as **environment
variables** overrides config. **No test guard catches it.**

⭐ **Test with `git var`, not an `env` grep.** An empty `env | grep ^GIT_` plus an empty `git log` on
a branch with no commits is **two empty results, not evidence.** Ask git what a commit *would* carry:

```bash
git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT       # -> Sam Rivera <sam@example.test>
git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT    # -> Sam Rivera <sam@example.test>
```

---

## 3 · The owner approves. Then, and only then:

```bash
git -C <repo> tag pre-merge/<scope>-$(date +%Y%m%d)  <shipping tip>     # safety, both cheap
git -C <repo> tag lane/<scope>-handover              origin/<lane>

git -C <repo> checkout <shipping-branch>
git -C <repo> merge --ff-only origin/<lane>     # ⛔ refuses rather than inventing a merge commit
git -C <repo> push origin <shipping-branch>     # ⛔ THE OWNER APPROVES THIS SEPARATELY
```

⭐ **`--ff-only` is deliberate** — the lane forked from the shipping tip and rebased back onto it, so
a fast-forward is always available. ⛔ **If it refuses, the lane did not rebase — send it back.
Never "fix" a refused ff-only with a merge commit.**
⚠ **Only the FIRST merge can fast-forward.** After that the tip has moved and every other lane
rebases. **That is the train working, not a fault.**

### ⭐ A METADATA-ONLY REWRITE IS PROVEN SAFE BY THE TREE HASH

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}     # before
git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}     # after  -> MUST match
git diff <old-sha> <new-sha>  # MUST be empty
```

⛔ **Never force-push a rewrite without this check first.**
⚠ **And do the authorship check BEFORE the merge** — a rewrite after the fact forces every held lane
to rebase twice, the second time over a history whose every SHA has moved.

---

## 4 · Every remaining lane then rebases — and PROVES its work survived

⛔ **This is the step that loses work.** A conflict resolution that takes the wrong side deletes a
lane's fix while leaving the branch, the commit and the green suite intact.

```bash
# 1 FINGERPRINT FIRST — you cannot prove survival without a before
git diff <old-base>..<old-head> | git patch-id --stable

git tag pre-rebase/<scope>-$(date +%Y%m%d)
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/<shipping-branch>       # ⛔ REBASE, NEVER MERGE

# 2 PROVE the change set is the same BYTES, not merely the same shape
git diff <new-base>..HEAD | git patch-id --stable             # MUST match

# 3 and prove it still WORKS
<suites>  +  re-run RED-FIRST on at least one arm per fix
git push --force-with-lease origin <lane>
```

⭐ **`patch-id` is strictly stronger than `--stat`:** `--stat` proves the change set is the same
SHAPE; `patch-id` proves it is the same BYTES. ⚠ **Still not sufficient alone** — it proves the bytes
arrived, not that they still work.

⛔⛔ **MEASURE, NEVER DERIVE — IN EITHER DIRECTION.** A base test count computed by
*subtracting* a lane's own delta from a measured total sends everyone chasing a phantom gap. When two
parties disagree on a total, **neither argues the total — both emit a PER-ITEM table and join them.**
Then **revert the production file** to settle *why*.

⚠ **A parametrised count is a function of the production code it parametrises over.** Checking out
the base TEST files while leaving production at HEAD **invents tests that never existed**.
⇒ **revert every file the commit touched, or skip the base and measure only HEAD.**
⭐ **A derived number that is internally consistent is more dangerous than one obviously wrong** —
it survives rounds of scepticism, because killing wrong hypotheses feels like evidence
for the next one.

**If the rebase reports a loss:** `git reset --hard pre-rebase/<scope>-<date>`, redo the resolution
deliberately, re-run. ⛔ **Do not hand over. Do not push over it.**

---

## 5 · The abort path — know it before you need it

| situation | recovery |
|---|---|
| `ff-only` refused | the lane has not rebased. **Send it back.** Never convert to a merge commit |
| merge landed, then found bad | `git reset --hard pre-merge/<scope>-<date>` **before pushing.** After pushing it is a revert commit and the owner's call |
| rebase dropped work | `git reset --hard pre-rebase/<scope>-<date>`, redo resolution |
| lane branch lost | ⭐ it is on the remote; `lane/<scope>-handover` tags the exact handover state |

⭐ **Five durability layers, and work has to fall through all five to be lost:**
lane WIP → pushed lane branch → handover tag → pre-merge tag → the shipping commit.

---

## 6 · ⛔ THE INTEGRATION TRAPS

1. ⛔⛔ **PAIRWISE-CLEAN IS NOT CLEAN.** Two CLEAN branches can merge to a `package.json` with two
   `workspaces` keys and **no conflict marker**. ⇒ **the gate runs on the MERGED tree; neither
   side's own green counts.**
2. ⛔ **Shared generated ledgers** (CI count pins — optional programme feature, off by default — manifests, registries) — ⛔ **no lane rebaselines
   them.** The integrating session does it **ONCE, on the merged tree**, and reads what the
   rebaseline tool does to any prose in that file before running it.
3. ⛔ **No `--amend`** once a finding, a decision record or a review cites a SHA. **An amended commit
   orphans its citations.**
4. ⛔ **Rebase the remaining lanes ONE AT A TIME**, not all at once, keeping the ledger correct at
   each step — then review and test the shipping branch itself before the next lane lands.
5. ⛔ **Release the shared resource before you merge.** Any merge run in a worktree a live app is serving
   moves the tree under it.
